items.title: George Lewis Interview, 1958-11-14
items.q: Herman Gessner. Well, then him, he was Spanish, German. And nothing but German. They called me and they speak to me in German

ctx.x: Well, it was nothing but French. And then the next day, it was maybe the Spanish class. Well, that was Capitano Chivarillo. Nothing but Spanish. Nothing. They speak to me in Spanish, the language of the class that was going on. And Herman Gessner. Herman Gessner teaches. That must be his grandson that is teaching at Tulane. Yes, I've heard that name. Yes, Herman Gessner. Well, then him, he was Spanish, German. And nothing but German. They called me and they speak to me in German and asked me things in German. No…
So you had to learn all of those languages too?

items.title: Alice Zeno Interview, 1960-01-25
items.q: and they speak nothing but that language of the class that did to me. And I used to laugh, ask me for water and tell me thank you

ctx.x: That's when we get out of the way. How many different languages could you read? Did you read German to you?

They read it to me. I was like all young people, foolish, giggling, wouldn't pay attention, wouldn't. But, you know, W.W. King. Yes. Gracie King. Yes. You know, they had a class all the week, every other day I believe, where Herman Gessner, which the one teaching there must be his grandson, and then Mrs. Verar and Charles Gaiare. Oh, yes. Mrs. Gerard and Charles Gaiare was French, and Capitaine de Chivarria was for Spanish, and Herman Gessner was German. So every other day they had a class, ladies would be there,…
You can understand Spanish then too? A little. Were there many Spanish people in the city when you were young that you remember?
